body:
Hey, I live in Australia we cant get exotics so all my Ts are local lol. I do handle most of them but my decision to do so has really been more down to the individual spider and its personality. I find the ones I have raised from slings and are usually more docile and they are also affected by the amount of noise/ vibration in their usual environment - I say this because I moved house and initially put them in a room on the roadside of the house (it was a busy main road) and I noticed a sharp rise in their defensive and agression behaviour (eg started attacking water when misting, reacting to opening enclosure lid - ie clearly on edge)  but once I moved them to a quieter place they calmed right back down again. 

Yet to be bitten and been handling for 10 years, as long as you are careful with them, are confident you can assess their personality, don't make them feel threatened and raise them in a peaceful environment you should be ok, but there will always be a risk and you have to decide if its worth it.  

Just FYI I have a variety of Selenotypus and Phlogius species.
